correctness.rationale: The exact tilt formula is \(|P(re^{it})|/P(r)\). If P has any nonreal zero, a conjugate upper-half-plane zero yields an interior zero at its polar angle for tilt log(radius). Nonincreasing nonnegative modulus would then vanish on an entire arc, impossible for a nonzero polynomial. All remaining roots are negative because the constant coefficient is positive and all coefficients nonnegative. Normalized linear factorization gives Bernoulli variables, whose independently tilted Fourier moduli are products of nonnegative nonincreasing factors. Arbitrary support gaps and the deterministic degree-zero case are covered. The rational quadratic witness establishes strictness of ordinary versus strong monotonicity. The exact-rational checker tests 10648 positive coefficient triples and independent factor examples; finite tests supplement but do not prove the universal theorem.

originality.rationale: The source paper introduces strong monotonicity and proves the Bernoulli forward inclusion but, in the inspected 2021 preprint and later author manuscript, does not establish its finite-support converse. The exact reverse implication from a nonreal polynomial root to a failing exponential tilt yields a complete classification by negative-real-root polynomials. value.rationale: A natural assumption needed for tilted local-limit estimates is fully classified on the entire class of finitely supported integer laws: it is exactly the translated Poisson-binomial class. The iff replaces a continuum of tilted Fourier monotonicity checks by the location of finitely many polynomial roots and gives a constructive spectral obstruction whenever it fails. The ordinary-but-not-strong three-point example demonstrates the genuine force of the classification. This is a complete natural structural classification, not a repackaging of the already-known Bernoulli sufficiency or an arbitrary finite slice. No infinite-support extension or new tail theorem is claimed.
